description: One node in a scene file: add, read, set, duplicate, reparent or delete it, paint TileMap cells, or bake a navigation region. Any ClassDB node type or script class can be added, so a NavigationRegion2D, an AnimationTree or a Camera3D is an add with that nodeType and its properties, and another scene is instanced by an add with instancePath. A set with properties {"name": "Boss"} renames a node, and answers nodePath as its new path. A rename or a reparent carries the node paths naming the node, as the editor's rename does: NodePath values on nodes (in arrays, dictionaries, built-in resources, %unique paths) and the tracks its players' animations hold, saving a library kept in a .tres of its own, and answers each rewrite under retargeted and each path it left under notRetargeted. The move is followed into every other .tscn that instances or inherits this scene at any depth: the editable children, values, added nodes and connections named by the old path are rewritten, since Godot finds a moved node's values by unique_id but editable children only by path and drops the values kept below them on the next save, and that scene's node paths and tracks are carried as above. A delete rewrites no path, and answers under stillNaming what named the deleted node and now names nothing. A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of one, so a texture, a material or a theme is a set like any other. A write is refused while the editor holds unsaved changes to the scene. A node this scene inherits takes values of this scene's own, and so does a node inside an instance of another scene once that instance's editableChildren is true; neither can be moved, renamed, copied or deleted, since the other scene makes it again on load. Through the editor when one serves the project; with none, a headless engine runs the editor's own tool and the answer says so under writtenBy, or readBy for a read. That engine runs every script of the file, where the editor runs only tool scripts, so what a script changes as the file loads or as a property is set is put back before anything is saved, and a file where that cannot be done, such as a scene whose script does not compile, is refused and nothing is written. Each file the written one refers to is named by its uid, as the editor names it, except a file the project's uid cache has no uid for yet (one made since the project was last scanned), which is named by path and listed under namedByPath with the call that scans it. An editor of the project that is running and has not reached this server is waited for rather than written around. Operations: add (needs nodeName): add a node of any class, or an instance of a scene; get (needs nodePath): read a node's class, path, properties and where its values come from, and a TileMapLayer's or TileMap's cells as set_tilemap_cells takes them, the first 1000 with cellCount for all. An instance of another scene also answers instanceOf and editableChildren, as scene_tree does; set (needs nodePath): set properties on a node, make the children of an instance editable, or put it in groups or take it out of them; give any of them together; duplicate (needs nodePath, newName): copy a node and its children, right after it or under parentNodePath, answering the copy's newNodePath, parentNodePath and index; reparent (needs nodePath, newParentPath): move a node under another parent, keeping where it is drawn, or to another place among its siblings; delete (needs nodePath): remove a node and its children; set_tilemap_cells (needs nodePath, cells): place tiles in a TileMapLayer or TileMap; bake_navigation (needs nodePath): bake a NavigationRegion2D or NavigationRegion3D from the geometry under it, as the editor's Bake button does, into the scene or its polygon's own file (savedTo); one holding none is given one (made). Answers polygons and vertices, with a note saying why when none came out, and meshesNote on the engine's mesh warning. It reads a script-free copy of the scene. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

addGroups.description: add and set: groups to put the node in, saved in this scene's file as the editor's Groups dock saves them. One it is in already is kept as it is. Only for ops add, set.

cells.description: Cells to place. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

atlasCoords.description: The tile in the source. Needed by every cell but an erased one.

sourceId.description: TileSet source id, or -1 to erase the cell.

editableChildren.description: set: on an instance of another scene, whether its children are editable here, as the editor's Editable Children makes them. True lets scene_node set give the nodes inside that instance values of this scene's own, which no other instance shares. An instance nested inside another takes it once the one around it has editable children. False drops every value this scene keeps for them, and every node it added below one of them. The answer names the nodes whose values went under droppedValues (they stay, with the instance's own values) and the added nodes that went under droppedNodes; a node added straight under the instance stays. The answer says editableChildren as the file now holds it. Only for op set.

includeDefaults.description: get: include properties still at their default. Default false. Only for op get.

index.description: add, duplicate and reparent: where the node goes among the parent's children, 0 for first. Default last, except for a copy under the original's own parent, which goes right after it. Child order is draw order in a CanvasItem and layout order in a Container. Only for ops add, duplicate, reparent.

instancePath.description: add: a scene to instance as the new node instead of a class, such as "ui/panel.tscn". It is saved as an instance of that file, the way the editor's Instantiate Child Scene saves one, so changes to that scene reach it; properties set its root. A scene that is the target or instances it is refused. Only for op add.

keepGlobalTransform.description: reparent: whether the node stays where it is drawn, its transform worked out again under the new parent, as the editor's reparent and Node.reparent keep it. A Control keeps its position only. A Node3D kept in place under a parent scaled unevenly across its turn ends up sheared, which no position, rotation and scale describe, and the answer then carries its transform under alsoChanged and says so under sheared. Default true; false keeps its own transform, so it moves with the new parent. Only for op reparent.

layer.description: set_tilemap_cells: the layer of a TileMap. Default 0. A TileMapLayer is one layer. Only for op set_tilemap_cells.

newName.description: duplicate: the copy's name. The copy has the nodes under the original and their connections, as the editor's Duplicate makes it: each connection keeps its flags, binds and unbinds, and one between two copied nodes joins the copies. Only for op duplicate.

newParentPath.description: reparent: the new parent, which may be the one it has, to move it among its siblings. In the scenes the move is followed into, the parent_id_path, from_uid_path and to_uid_path saved beside each rewritten path are dropped, since their ids ran through the old parent; the node's own unique_id is kept, and the next save writes the dropped ones again. Only for op reparent.

nodeName.description: add: the new node's name. Only for op add.

nodePath.description: Node path from the scene root, such as "Player/Sprite2D". "." is the root. Only for ops get, set, duplicate, reparent, delete, set_tilemap_cells, bake_navigation.

nodeType.description: add: the node class, such as "CharacterBody2D", or a class_name a project script declares, which the node is made as with that script attached. Give this or instancePath. The answer names the node made as get does: nodeType its engine class, for an instance the class of its scene's root, with scriptClass when its script declares a class_name. With no editor open, a class_name the class cache does not list yet is put in it first, and classCacheRebuilt says so. Only for op add.

parentNodePath.description: add: where the node goes. Default the root. duplicate: where the copy goes. Only for ops add, duplicate.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

properties.description: Properties to set, keyed by Godot property name. Vectors, colours and the like may be written as {"x": 1, "y": 2} or tagged {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 1, "y": 2}, which is the form a read answers with, so a value read off one node can be written straight to another. One carrying a field its type has not, such as a z for a Vector2, is refused naming it. A colour may also be given as its html code, "#ff8000" or "#ff800080". A key may also be a colon path into one of the components of a vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform, as GDScript names them, so one axis is written alone: "position:x", "modulate:a", "region_rect:size:y"; a component the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A property holding a node takes the path to it from the node being set, such as "../Player". A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of a file, which a read answers with its class and, when its script declares one, scriptClass, or a resource built into the scene as {"_type": "CircleShape2D", "radius": 8}, its class (an engine class or a script's class_name) beside its properties. A typed list or map of resources or nodes, such as Array[Item], takes each in the same forms, a node by its path; a read answers a resource built into the scene in that form, with what it holds away from the defaults, so it too can be written to another node. script takes the res:// path of a script to attach, one with no class_name included, and is attached before the rest are set, so the properties it declares can be given beside it. Each value is read back once set, and one the engine changed or refused is refused with what it holds. An enum property takes its number or the name of a value: as the script spells it, as the inspector shows it, or for an engine enum as its constant, so Add or BLEND_MODE_ADD, and Bottom or VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_BOTTOM for a global one; a value past an export range, or a number no value of an enum has, is written as given and named under outsideDeclared. A key may reach into a resource built into this one: the property holding it, a slash, then one of its own, so a TileSet's first atlas source takes "sources/0/0:0/0/probability". A list of such resources is stepped into by an element's index, so "lines/1/text" is the text of the second resource in lines and the others are left as they were. A resource kept in a file of its own, or built into the scene an instance comes from, is written in that file, or replaced here by one of this file's own. The next element of a list is made by writing to it, as the inspector's Add Element makes it: physics_layer_0/collision_layer on a TileSet with no physics layer makes its first, and "sources/0/0:0/0/physics_layer_0/polygon_0/points" a tile's first collision polygon on that layer. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. Only for ops add, set.

removeGroups.description: set: groups to take the node out of. One it is not in is refused, and so is one another scene puts it in (the scene that makes it, instances it or is inherited here), which only that scene can take it out of. Only for op set.

scenePath.description: Scene file inside the project, such as "scenes/main.tscn" or "res://scenes/main.tscn".

name: scene_node
title: Scene nodes
